topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the lecture's core themes on cancer evolution, cell of origin, and the influence of the tumor microenvironment.

topics.label: Darwinian clonal selection and mutation accumulation
topics.groupedBecause: It illustrates how successive genetic mutations provide competitive growth advantages that drive Darwinian clonal expansion in tissues.

topics.label: Epigenetic alterations in tumor initiation
topics.groupedBecause: It demonstrates how transient chromatin changes and altered transcriptional states can initiate tumor development independently of genetic mutations.

topics.label: Cell of origin and stem cell hierarchies in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: They investigate how tissue stem cell properties and the specific differentiation state of the cell of origin influence malignant transformation.

topics.label: Microenvironmental and inflammatory drivers of cancer progression
topics.groupedBecause: They show that inflammatory signals and supportive stroma within the microenvironment are essential for both incipient tumor outgrowth and established tumor maintenance.

topics.label: Technologies for analyzing tumor evolution and the microenvironment
topics.groupedBecause: It describes the single-cell sequencing and spatial omics technologies used to map mutational timing, cell plasticity, and microenvironmental interactions in tumors.

topics.label: Synthesis of multi-factorial cancer evolution and conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: They integrate the combined contributions of mutations, epigenetics, cell of origin, and microenvironment to cancer evolution before closing the lecture.
